events.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump may be looking to wind down Iran conflict behind smokescreen of military options
The US seems to be scaling back its naval presence in the Arabian Sea, raising questions about President Donald Trump's alternative plans for the region.
👉 [The USS George Washington ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77978)aircraft carrier left the Middle East on November 18 after spending three months on station. It is returning to Yokosuka, Japan, with its strike group. Yokosuka is home to the US 7th Fleet. Previously, it had been deployed[ in the Arabian Sea](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77830) alongside the USS Theodore Roosevelt, which arrived in the region on November 15, and the USS George H.W. Bush, which arrived in April. Judging by the INSS interactive map, American warships are keeping their distance from the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf.
Reducing the US carrier presence in the region is an interesting choice after Washington assembled its largest naval force there since 2003, US analyst Brandon Weichert writes.
The departure of the USS George Washington also coincided with the APEC summit, where US President Donald Trump joined his Russian and Chinese counterparts at [the negotiating table](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78007.).
❗️Both Russia and China have long advocated a diplomatic solution to the Gulf crisis. At the summit, Trump signaled his interest in lasting peace in the region, prompting some observers to believe that he is considering "an alternative to massive escalation."
Meanwhile, US hawks and Israeli politicians are pressing him to resume the war with Iran. Last week in Washington, Gofman advocated joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran during meetings with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and US envoy Steve Witkoff.
👉 On November 18, US CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper held a trilateral meeting with IDF Chief of Staff Gen. Eyal Zamir and Mossad Director Roman Gofman in Tel Aviv to conduct an Iran threat assessment. On November 19, Axios reported that Trump had tasked the Pentagon and US intelligence agencies with assessing Iran’s possible responses to CENTCOM’s military strike scenarios.
Still, Weichert believes Trump is using security discussions as a smokescreen while scaling back the US naval presence and delaying any major escalation, largely due to depleted military stockpiles and incapability of decisively winning a war with Iran.

🇮🇷🛢 Iran war sets the stage for permanently high oil prices
 
Perpetually higher crude prices of $85-95 a barrel are “poised to be the reality for the foreseeable future” thanks to the never-ending security crisis in the Persian Gulf, according to a new WSJ report citing production, inventory and price data correlated with tanker attacks, rising shipping costs, and efforts by producers to bypass the Hormuz Strait.
 
The data shows:
🔴 a growing number of attacks on tankers trying to slip past Iran’s Hormuz maritime traffic control regimen, with November’s figures already the highest among any month except October and a week-and-a-half still left in the month
🔴 skyrocketing shipping costs for Gulf oil (five times prewar levels)
🔴 month after month of falling global crude inventories
🔴 mega-buyer[ China’s return](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77207) to the market after months of self-imposed restrictions on crude purchases intended to stabilize prices and inventories
 
Long term, permanently high oil prices mean[ ‘higher everything prices’ ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75711)for consumers, industrial and agricultural producers, plus inflation and higher interest rates, slowing demand and trade. For net energy importers like Europe, the Iran war adds fuel to the process of deindustrialization going on since 2022 and the start of the Ukraine conflict.

🚀 New underground missile city spotted in central Iran
 
OSINT observers looking at commercial geospatial satellite data have spotted the construction of a new underground facility burrowed deep into a mountain range in Isfahan province, central Iran.
A PlanetLabs timelapse from January through November 2026 shows the creation of roads, a construction support camp, concrete production and materials storage sites, and excavation of at least five tunnels, together with large spoil pile.
ArmsControlWonk says judging by the construction activity and local geography, the site appears to be a new IRGC missile base, with potential for tunnels up to 150-200M deep – [unreachable](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76457) even by direct hits using all known conventional and nuclear weapons.
OSINT evidence on the new facility follows Iran’s unveiling of a separate new missile city equipped with heavy ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles, drones and[ a “surprise” weapon](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77627) blurred in reporting, and underground roads wide enough to comfortably fit multiple tractor trailers side by side.
Iran’s Zagros Mountains, missile cities and equally sophisticated [undersea tunnels](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68832) and coastal staging areas have been credited as the big reasons the US and Israel have proven unable to substantively degrade the nation’s counterstrike capabilities in the course of the 2025 and 2026 wars.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇾🇪Houthis reveal their next targets: five pieces of critical Saudi economic infrastructure
 
Yemen’s Ansar Allah fighters painted large red targeting reticles on infrastructure across Saudi Arabia on Friday, including:
➡️ four of the kingdom’s biggest ports (King Fahd Industrial Port, Jazan Port, Yanbu Port, Jeddah Port)
➡️ The King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh ([already subject to repeated attacks this week](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78028))
The Ansar Allah-aligned Yemeni Armed Forces warned in a statement that Saudi ports would “become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats to bombard the Port of Hodeidah.”
💬“We warn all staff, workers and those present in or near these facilities to evacuate immediately and keep their distance. Furthermore, we call on all shipping companies to remove their vessels from these ports without delay,” the Houthis urged.
Declaring Riyadh’s Financial Center a legitimate military target, the group similarly advised “all employees, workers and citizens” to evacuate to avoid harm.
Separately, the fighters warned that “in response to the Saudi enemy’s targeting of power stations in Saada and Mokha…the Al Shuqaiq Power Station will be a legitimate target of our forces in the coming hours.” A similar advisory to evacuate was given.
Finally, Ansar Allah warned commercial airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe and “will become a theater for our operations in the coming hours – with the exception of the sacred airspace over Mecca and Medina.”
The Houthis’ new strategy of warning about the enemy sites they plan to hit echoes that of Iran during recent wars with Israel and the US, when the IRGC issued advisories in locations where targets were situated near civilian areas. The advance warning also appears to signal a newfound confidence in its missile and drone operations’ ability to reach their intended targets amid [dwindling enemy air defenses](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76454).
